No cross-chain-specific ABI — this is calldata for any contract call.
SEND — STATICCALL FOR A READ
YOU
.staticcall(data)
proxyAddress

Same syntax as calling any contract — the proxy has no matching function, so the fallback catches it.
YOUR FRAME DECIDES THE PATH — NOT view
A tstore probe halts only inside a static frame, so the path is read off your frame, not the callee’s view: staticcall → staticCrossChainCall, plain call → executeCrossChainCall.
USE THE ANSWER — A VALUE, NOT A RECEIPT
EEZ manager
staticCrossChainCall
returns
entry.returnData
returns
abi.decode(ret, (uint256))
→
have ≥ need · credited[user] += need
have < need · shortfall[user] = need - have
The manager returns the entry's pre-computed returnData; balanceOf ran on the other rollup, with your contract's proxy as msg.sender, when the composer built the entry. Decode it like any same-chain read, then branch.
AND ONLY WHERE AN ENTRY ALREADY EXISTS
The composer wrote the entry before your call ran, and it resolves only in the block where its rollup was verified (L1) or its table was loaded (L2) — ExecutionNotInCurrentBlock on both; an L1 static entry must also still match its state roots. A miss — EntryNotFound on L2, ExecutionNotFound on L1 — looks like the destination reverting to a caller that checks only ok. The forwarded revert data usually tells them apart, but a destination can emit the same selector, so don't branch on it.

DAPP DEVELOPERS

How to call a contract on another rollup

The Quickstart used a call's return value in card 00 and card 02, through a plain call to increment(). This card is the read-only variant: send it as a staticcall so it resolves a static entry, then decode the answer and branch on it.

You send it to the proxy address, and the proxy's fallback catches everything. Send it as a staticcall and the answer comes back as return data you decode and branch on, inside the same transaction.

WHAT YOU'LL LEARN
  • 01 · ENCODE IT LIKE ANY CALLA normal call, encoded with no cross-chain-specific ABI.
  • 02 · STATICCALL FOR READSYour frame picks the path: a staticcall resolves a static entry, a plain call an execution entry. Use staticcall for reads, so the entry is read-only.
  • 03 · DECODE IT AND BRANCHWhat comes back is a value, not a receipt — decode it and let it decide what the transaction does.
